title: Telescopic cascode OTA
description: A single-ended telescopic cascode, drawn at rest: an input pair, an input (NMOS) cascode, a load (PMOS) cascode and a cascoded current-mirror load stacked between the rails, plus the tail and the bias reference it copies. The feedback the application closes around it holds the output at $V_{out,dc}$, and the two inputs sit apart by whatever offset that takes. The mirror is the low-voltage kind: its two devices share a gate, and that gate is the diode side's output node — the drain of the diode side's PMOS cascode, where its NMOS cascode's drain meets it — so that node sits one mirror $V_{GS}$ below the supply while the output sits at $V_{out,dc}$. The two sides of the stack therefore do not sit at the same voltages, and every device is drawn on its own side. The currents are stated the way the circuit sets them: only the bias reference is programmed, with $I_{tail}$; the tail device shares its gate and width and delivers the programmed current less the mirror's drain-voltage error; the pair's two transistors are one width, each carrying its own share of what the tail delivers; each cascode carries the current of the pair transistor under it; the mirror's diode side carries the diode-side current, and its output side shares its gate and width, so what it returns to the output is read from the table at its own drain voltage. The share is solved so that the currents at the output node balance, and the difference between the two pair transistors' gate-source voltages is reported as the systematic offset. Cascoding multiplies each side's output resistance by the cascode intrinsic gain, so $A_v = g_{m,pair} * R_{out}$ with $R_{out}$ = par(NMOS side, PMOS side) and each side's $R_{out} \approx A_{v0,casc} / g_{ds}$ of the device it cascodes, all read on the output side. That is the topology's headline: the highest single-stage gain per unit current, bought with output-swing headroom — the four stacked $V_{dsat}$ plus the tail eat the rail. The stack is parameterized by its NODES, not by per-device drops: the tail node is solved so the produced $CM_{in}$ equals $CM_{dc}$; the output side's two internal nodes $V_a$ (pair drain / NMOS-cascode source) and $V_b$ (mirror drain / PMOS-cascode source) are choice params, and the gates above them are the bias lines both sides share; the diode side's two internal nodes are solved under those same gates. Every device $V_{DS}$ is then a subtraction between adjacent nodes and every source-above-bulk device carries its true body bias. The cascode-pole and settling behaviour is estimate-grade; sim owns sign-off.

params.name: Av_target
params.note: DC gain target: 300 (about 50 dB) is what one cascoded stage reaches at these lengths without gain boosting, about 8-bit static accuracy in unity feedback, the class of a switched-capacitor integrator or sample-and-hold of moderate precision. An example, to be replaced with the design's own spec

params.name: GBW_target
params.note: unity-gain bandwidth target into the 2 pF load: a single-stage OTA with a 20 uA tail at moderate inversion lands in the high single-digit megahertz. An example, to be replaced with the design's own spec

params.name: SR_target
params.note: slew-rate target: the tail current into the 2 pF load; 5 V/us moves a 0.5 V step in 100 ns, the range of a low-power single-stage OTA at a 20 uA tail. An example, to be replaced with the design's own spec

params.name: vn_target
params.note: input-referred thermal density budget. The row (pair plus load mirror) reads each device's noise from the tables where they carry it: near 27.1 nV/rtHz on a sky130 tt realization with the PMOS devices on the pfet table, just over this budget. No simulated floor exists for this topology

params.name: vos_target
params.note: input offset budget, 1 sigma; half-micron devices at these currents put the Pelgrom spread near 6.5 mV with a generic coefficient — shrinking this budget is what forces area

params.name: swing_target
params.note: required single-ended output swing (peak) about the output DC — the telescopic's scarcest resource; the swing row computes what the placed nodes leave

params.name: CM_lo
params.note: input CM range the application presents, low edge — checked exactly by the cm-lo edge at every evaluation (the sweep put the widest closing range at 0.92-1.21 V on a sky130 tt realization with the PMOS devices on the pfet table, at the shipped choices: below it the tail device leaves saturation, above it the gain falls short). The edge checks the ENDPOINT; the interior is the sweep's to show

params.name: CM_hi
params.note: input CM range the application presents, high edge — its ENDPOINT checked by the cm-hi edge the same way

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: the input common mode the application presents. The engine places the tail node so the sheet sits exactly here; sweep it to trace the common-mode axis. The slider stops where the stack does: with V_a holding the pair's drain low, the tail node cannot climb past its range and the topology genuinely cannot take a higher CM — the telescopic's known input-range ceiling

params.name: V_tail
params.note: the tail node — the pair's source. Solved rather than set: searched between min and max (the range it is searched in, not slider bounds) until the produced common mode equals CM_dc. An end of the range where the relation does not evaluate — the top end, where it leaves the pair too little room below V_a to size — is stepped inward silently, and the searched range is reported only if the search then fails; the input device declares that it must stay saturated, so its own saturation check owns that

params.name: V_a
params.note: the output side's NMOS internal node: the output-side pair transistor's drain and its cascode's source. Set by the cascode gate bias in silicon; here a direct choice — that pair transistor's vds is V_a - V_tail and its cascode's is V_out_dc - V_a, by construction. The gate above it, V_a plus that cascode's vgs, is the bias line both NMOS cascodes share. Stated at this design point. Where the design is held fixed (a range end), the gate bias above this node is what stays put and the node is re-solved under it, between min and max.

params.name: V_b
params.note: the output side's PMOS internal node: the mirror output device's drain and the output-side load cascode's source. That mirror device's vds is VDD - V_b and its cascode's is V_b - V_out_dc, by construction. The gate below it, V_b less that cascode's vgs, is the bias line both PMOS cascodes share, and the diode side's node under that gate has to clear the mirror's gate, one mirror V_GS below the supply, by the diode-side cascode's saturation voltage — the default sits high for that. Stated at this design point. Where the design is held fixed (a range end), the gate bias above this node is what stays put and the node is re-solved under it, between min and max.

params.name: V_ar
params.note: the diode side's NMOS internal node: the diode-side pair transistor's drain and its cascode's source. Solved, not set: the two NMOS cascodes share one gate, so this is the node that hangs the diode-side cascode's own gate-source voltage under that gate. It differs from V_a by the difference between the two cascodes' gate-source voltages, which carry different currents at different drain voltages. Searched between min and max; the stored value is never read

params.name: V_br
params.note: the diode side's PMOS internal node: the mirror diode side's drain and the diode-side load cascode's source. Solved, not set: the two PMOS cascodes share one gate, so this is the node that sits the diode-side cascode's own gate-source voltage above that gate. Searched between min and max; the stored value is never read

params.name: out_share
params.note: the share of the tail current the pair's output-side transistor carries at rest — solved, not set. The output is a high-impedance node that the feedback around the amplifier holds at V_out_dc, so in the resting circuit the current that branch carries down is exactly the current the mirror's output side returns: the engine searches for the share at which the two are equal, the current law at the output node. The diode-side transistor carries the rest, so the two add up to what the tail delivers by construction. It is searched between 0.01 and 0.99; the stored value is never read

params.name: V_out_dc
params.note: output DC level; the NMOS drops below it and the PMOS drops above it must each close the rail. The NMOS and PMOS cascodes meet at a high-impedance output that nothing on this sheet holds; the feedback the application closes around the amplifier holds it here

params.name: avt
params.note: Pelgrom A_VT

params.name: abeta
params.note: Pelgrom A_beta

params.name: sign_p
params.note: vds sign convention of the PMOS-side tables: +1 for an N-style axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis. The mirror's diode side needs it too: its drain is not its gate. Read both sides of each PMOS pair from the same table: the gate voltage they share is passed in that table's convention

params.name: I_tail
params.note: the current the bias reference is programmed to — the one current on this sheet that is typed. The tail device mirrors it 1:1 through the shared gate and delivers it less the mirror's drain-voltage error (the tail node sits below the reference's diode drop); slew rate and supply current are computed from what is delivered, not from this number

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion, set on the output-side transistor; its partner copies its width and carries the rest of the tail current. Sets gm per current and the input-referred noise

params.name: gm_id_casc
params.note: cascode-device inversion, set on the two output-side cascodes; the diode-side cascodes copy their widths. Higher gm/ID lifts the cascode gain av0_casc but costs vdsat headroom

params.name: gm_id_mir
params.note: load-mirror inversion, set on the diode side and inherited by the output side through the shared gate: lower gm/ID adds less noise and offset, but the mirror's gate is the diode side's output node, one mirror V_GS below the supply, and the diode side's NMOS cascode needs its saturation voltage between that node and V_a — at 8 a PMOS table's V_GS leaves it in triode, so the default sits at 13

params.name: gm_id_tail
params.note: inversion level of the bias reference, which the tail device inherits through the shared gate: a higher V* costs headroom at the tail node

params.name: L_tail
params.note: length of the bias reference and of the tail device, which mirror at one length: longer shrinks the mirror's drain-voltage error

doc.title: Tail bias reference
doc.description: The diode-connected reference the programmed current $I_{tail}$ flows into — the one device on this sheet whose current is typed. Its drain is its gate, so its $V_{DS}$ is its own $V_{GS}$ and the table is read along that diagonal with nothing estimated. It publishes its width and its gate voltage, which is all the tail device needs to copy it.

doc.title: Tail current source
doc.description: The tail device, on the bias reference's gate at the reference's width: a 1:1 mirror of the programmed current, with $V_{tail}$ as its drain-source voltage. Its current is read off the table rather than typed — the reference sits at its own diode drop and this device at $V_{tail}$, so it delivers the programmed current scaled by what that difference in $V_{DS}$ does through its $g_{ds}$. It has to stay saturated, and it leaves saturation when $V_{tail}$ falls below its own $V_{dsat}$, which is what sets the low end of the usable common-mode range.

params.name: W_t
params.note: the bias reference's width — a 1:1 copy

params.name: vgs_t
params.note: the bias reference's gate voltage — the gate wire the two share

params.name: vds_t
params.note: the tail node

doc.title: Input-pair device, output side
doc.description: The pair transistor under the output-side cascode, sized at its share of what the tail delivers; its ro sets the NMOS-side cascoded output resistance. Its source sits at the tail node (its body bias) and its drain at V_a. It publishes its width, which its partner on the diode side copies, and its gate-source voltage, which differs from its partner's by the input offset that holds the output where it is.

doc.title: Input (NMOS) cascode
doc.description: The output side's NMOS cascode; its intrinsic gain av0 multiplies the output-side pair transistor's ro to set the NMOS-side Rout. It is in that transistor's branch and carries its current. Its source stands on the internal node V_a, so that is its body bias. It publishes its width, which the diode-side cascode copies.

doc.title: Load (PMOS) cascode
doc.description: The output side's PMOS cascode; its intrinsic gain av0 multiplies the mirror output device's ro to set the PMOS-side Rout. It is in the output-side pair transistor's branch and carries its current. Its source stands on the internal node V_b, below the bulk at VDD, so its body bias is VDD - V_b (the PMOS tables' vsb axis carries that magnitude). It publishes its width, which the diode-side cascode copies.

doc.title: Load mirror device, diode side
doc.description: The diode side of the PMOS load mirror. It carries the current of the pair transistor at the bottom of its branch — what the tail delivers less the output-side transistor's share — and its gate is the diode side's output node, the drain of the cascode above its own drain. That puts the node one $V_{GS}$ below the supply, and the mirror's shared gate there: its width and gate voltage are what the output side copies. Its drain is the diode side's PMOS internal node.

doc.title: Load mirror device, output side
doc.description: The output side of the PMOS load mirror, on the diode side's gate at the diode side's width; its ro, cascoded by the output-side PMOS cascode, sets the PMOS-side output resistance. Its drain is V_b, so its current is read off the table at that drain voltage rather than typed: wherever V_b does not sit where the diode side's drain does, it differs from the diode side's, and the share the output-side pair transistor carries follows it.

params.name: W_m
params.note: the diode side's width — a 1:1 copy

params.name: vgs_m
params.note: the diode side's gate voltage — the gate the two share, in the sign convention of the diode side's table

doc.title: Input-pair device, diode side
doc.description: The pair transistor under the diode-side cascode: the output-side transistor's width, carrying the rest of what the tail delivers. A matched pair is one width, so its width is copied, and its current is given, which makes this a width-and-current sizing: the table is inverted at that current density for the gate-source voltage it takes. Its body bias is the tail node, like its partner's, and its drain is the diode side's NMOS internal node. Wherever its current or its drain differs from its partner's, so does its gate-source voltage, and that difference is the input offset the sheet reports.

params.name: W_i
params.note: the output-side transistor's width — a matched pair

params.name: I_side
params.note: what the tail delivers less the output-side transistor's share

params.name: vds_i
params.note: from the tail node up to the diode side's NMOS internal node

doc.title: Input (NMOS) cascode, diode side
doc.description: The diode side's NMOS cascode: the output-side cascode's width, on the gate the two share, carrying the diode-side pair transistor's current. Its drain is the diode side's output node — the mirror's gate, one mirror $V_{GS}$ below the supply — rather than the output, so it sits at a different drain voltage from its partner, and its gate-source voltage is read off the table at its own current and drain voltage. The node under it is solved so that this gate-source voltage hangs it under the shared gate.

params.name: W_c
params.note: the output-side cascode's width

doc.title: Load (PMOS) cascode, diode side
doc.description: The diode side's PMOS cascode: the output-side cascode's width, on the gate the two share, carrying the diode-side current. Its drain is the diode side's output node, which is the mirror's gate, so its drain-source voltage is what is left between its source and one mirror $V_{GS}$ below the supply. The node above it is solved so that its gate-source voltage sits it above the shared gate. Its body bias is VDD less that node (the PMOS tables' vsb axis carries that magnitude).

params.name: W_c
params.note: the output-side cascode's width

equations.name: CM_in
equations.note: the input common mode this bias produces — an OUTPUT here, not a setting: the tail node plus the mean of the two pair transistors' gate-source voltages, the level the two inputs sit about. It rises monotonically with the tail node, so the pin is a well-posed one-unknown search

equations.name: tail_headroom
equations.note: how far the tail node sits above the tail device's saturation edge — exact, because the tail node is the variable rather than something inferred from a common mode

equations.name: gm_pair
equations.note: the pair's transconductance into the output node. Each pair transistor turns half the differential input into current, which its cascode passes up unchanged: the diode-side half reaches the output through the load mirror, whose current gain is its output device's $g_m$ over its diode device's, and the output-side half arrives directly. It is either transistor's own $g_m$ where the two sides sit at the same levels

equations.name: Rout_n
equations.note: NMOS-side output resistance: the output-side pair transistor's ro boosted by its cascode's intrinsic gain

equations.name: Rout_p
equations.note: PMOS-side output resistance: the mirror output device's ro boosted by the output-side load cascode's intrinsic gain

equations.name: Rout
equations.note: the two cascoded sides in parallel. The gain assumes a capacitive load, so nothing here models a resistive one; this row is what a composing parent checks its own loading against

equations.name: Av
equations.note: single-stage telescopic gain: the pair's transconductance into the output resistance, both sides of which are read at the output node

equations.name: SR
equations.note: the whole tail current steered into the load — the current the tail device delivers, not the number the reference is programmed to

equations.name: vn_in
equations.note: both pair transistors and both mirror devices, each at its own density: a pair transistor's noise is in series with its own input, so it enters as it is; a mirror device's is a current at the output, referred back through the pair's transconductance. The diode side's noise current reaches the output through the load mirror, as the diode side's half of the signal does in gm_pair, so its gm is multiplied by the mirror's gain gm_mir/gm_mirr, which leaves gm_mir. Each side is read separately because the two sides sit at different drain voltages. The cascodes add little (they carry the same current at low gm relative to the pair)

equations.name: vos
equations.expr: sqrt((pelgrom_vos(avt, abeta, in__W, L_in, inr__gm/inr__id)^2 + pelgrom_vos(avt, abeta, in__W, L_in, in__gm/in__id)^2)/2 + (pelgrom_vos(avt, abeta, mirr__W, L_mir, gm_id_mir)*mirr__gm/gm_pair)^2)
equations.note: random offset, 1 sigma: the input pair's offset plus the mirror pair's offset referred through the pair's transconductance. Each pair transistor contributes half of a matched pair's variance at its own gm/ID — the two share a width but not a current. The mirror pair is read at the diode side, whose width the output side copies

equations.name: vos_sys
equations.note: input-referred systematic offset — the difference of the two pair transistors' gate-source voltages at rest, read directly: the input offset the feedback holding the output at $V_{out,dc}$ has to apply. The mirror's output side sits at V_b and its diode side at the diode side's own node, so the two return different currents, and the pair's two transistors carry different shares; the cascodes shield the pair's drains, so the two drains differ only by the difference between the two NMOS cascodes' gate-source voltages. Reported only; no check reads it

equations.name: swing
equations.note: peak-to-peak output swing the PLACED nodes actually leave, symmetric about the output DC: the output can fall to V_a plus the NMOS cascode's vdsat and rise to V_b minus the PMOS cascode's — the idealized stacked-vdsat budget read ~3x optimistic once the nodes were explicit. Push V_a down and V_b up to widen it

equations.name: cgg_in
equations.note: estimate: the capacitance one input terminal presents — the gate capacitance of a single pair transistor, as the mean of the two, which differ a little because their currents do. Gate capacitance only, because the Miller term needs the gate-drain fraction and these tables do not carry it, so a driving stage sees more than this. No rule reads it

equations.name: I_q
equations.note: estimate: quiescent supply current — the current the tail device delivers is the whole of it: the cascodes and the mirror load carry it in the two branches above the pair. The reference branch that programs it is shared bias infrastructure and is not counted here. The datasheet line for comparing designs; no rule reads it

checks.note: reads each device's thermal noise from the table where the table carries it, and the gamma = 1 estimate where it does not; it stays advisory because a sheet cannot know which table it will be evaluated on, and the simulator owns noise sign-off
the stacked headroom must leave at least the peak-to-peak output swing
the common mode this bias produces has to sit inside the range the application presents
paired with cm-not-below; the cm-lo/cm-hi edges check that the design covers the range ENDS, and the CM_dc sweep shows the whole landscape

operatingRange.name: cm-lo
operatingRange.note: the claimed low edge, checked exactly: the whole sheet re-evaluates at CM_dc = CM_lo on the design this run produced — its own tail-node solve over its full range, every device held at the geometry it was sized to — and every hard rule must hold there

operatingRange.name: cm-hi
operatingRange.note: the claimed high edge, checked the same way. The edges check the ENDPOINTS; the CM_dc sweep remains the authority on the full landscape
